Ban on employer use of automated decision systems.

reading.body:
Indiana's AI-related legislative activity in this dataset is dominated by harm-containment bills, with only one measure, HB1421, directly targeting an AI system, specifically a ban on employer use of automated decision systems.

The eleven bills span from December 2025 through March 2026. The clearest cluster addresses digital sexual image abuse, covered by two parallel House bills introduced on the same day. A second cluster covers health care and insurance, with three bills in that space. Two bills address foreign adversaries and foreign agent registration. One bill, SB0083, concerns utility matters, which could touch power infrastructure, but the title alone does not establish that connection, and the data does not develop it.

The automated decision systems bill is the only one that speaks to AI deployment directly. The rest address outputs or contexts where AI may be involved, without naming it. The data does not include bill text, committee status, vote outcomes, or whether any bill became law. A reader cannot determine from this dataset how Indiana's regulatory posture compares to other states, or whether any of these measures would meaningfully constrain or redirect AI compute investment in the state.
